questions.q: What does the Show Me filter control?
options: Which columns appear in the report
Whose records are included, such as all, mine, or my team's
The chart type used on a dashboard
The order in which groups are sorted
questions.explain: Show Me is the record scope filter. It works together with sharing rules, so it never exposes records you lack access to.

questions.q: Why is a relative date range such as Current Fiscal Quarter useful in a saved report?
options: It locks the report to one specific quarter forever
It removes the need for a Show Me filter
It bypasses field-level security
It moves with today's date, so the report stays current
questions.explain: Relative ranges are recalculated each time the report runs, so the same saved report stays correct as time passes.

questions.q: What does a locked filter do?
options: Prevents people who run the report from changing or removing it
Hides the report from all dashboards
Encrypts the data in the filtered field
Forces the report to become a joined report
questions.explain: A locked filter (shown with a padlock) can't be changed by viewers, which protects conditions that define what the report means.

questions.q: You add three field filters to a report without changing any filter logic. How are they combined?
options: With OR
Only the first filter is applied
With AND
They are applied in random order
questions.explain: Field filters combine with AND by default. Custom filter logic (covered later in this chapter) lets you introduce OR.

questions.q: A report you just built says "No records returned". Which is a sensible first check?
options: Delete the report type
Review the date filter and other filters for something too restrictive
Convert the report to Matrix
Add more columns
questions.explain: Overly narrow filters are the most common cause. The date range and picklist values are the usual suspects.
